## File Atom Card (FA)

A small inline reference to a file: type icon, name, extension.

It is meant to sit **inside prose** and inside a custom summary line, so it deliberately does two things no other shell does:

- **mounts no domain renderer** — there is no preview, no waveform, no thumbnail
- **takes no more vertical space than the text around it**

That is the whole design. An atom that grew a thumbnail would break the line height of every paragraph that mentions a file, and an atom that booted a renderer would make a sentence containing five file references pay for five decoders.

At 70 lines it is the smallest of the four shells, and that is the point: everything a file reference needs inline, nothing it does not.

### The family this belongs to

Five pieces make up how a file renders in Boxel:

| Piece | Job |
|---|---|
| `file-shell-atom` | inline reference — icon, name, extension |
| `file-shell-embedded` | complete content, flowing inside a document |
| `file-shell-fitted` | the parent-sized collection cell |
| `file-shell-isolated` | the full work surface |
| `file-preview-stage` | the slot all four project into; owns loading, failure, provenance |

A shell never knows how to draw a PDF, a waveform or a 3D scene. It renders the
stage, and the stage hands the remaining space to the family's own renderer,
declared by a FileDef subclass as `static previewComponent`. A file whose family
has no renderer yet gets an honest generic pane rather than a broken one.
